prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a finished, extremely polished desktop WEB APP interface for BirdRadar, landscape 1536x1024. Edge-to-edge actual screen design, no computer device, no perspective frame, no marketing poster. First reference image is MATERIAL ONLY: luminous translucent milky silicone / latex film, cyan, lilac, ice blue, pale rose, thin gold fringes, silky microscopic line detail and transparent overlapping layers. Translate it into GEOGRAPHIC migration-density fields conforming to a real map, never a floating abstract sculpture. Second reference is existing bird stamp ART DIRECTION: perforated cream paper edge, dark botanical stamp, a bird as focal artwork. Upgrade stamp printing with prismatic Balatro-inspired holographic foil, embossed metallic outlines, tasteful diffraction and angle highlights; maintain bird identity and crisp typography. UI chrome is quiet matte midnight blue; reserve iridescence for the geographic heat field and stamps. Readable clean humanist sans typography, editorial serif for bird names, precise generous spacing. No neon cyberpunk, no generic dashboard card grid, no big metrics, no made-up live data. Keep coastline, relief and fine country/city labels readable THROUGH heat layers. The route core is denser/milkier, periphery semitransparent, overlapping ribbons form pale luminous interference. Some tiny flowing particles follow the corridor. Distinguish colours using a small legend. This is a conceptual visualization, not a scientific plot: include a clearly readable bottom note exactly "Concept preview · illustrative heat field". Real data provenance text can say "Historical tracking · Movebank". Main navigation: "BirdRadar" then "Explore", "Stamps", "Lights Out", "About". Every image must show a complete usable composition with species selector, map controls, timeline and stamp content. No watermark. COMPOSITION B — Atlas and collector side by side. Shared 72px header. Below, divide screen into a spacious LEFT 68% interactive dark topographic Europe–Africa map and RIGHT 32% refined slate-black stamp collector panel. Main title at top-left "Migration atlas" with "White stork" dropdown and small "Historical tracking" badge. Map not globe: geographic relief, coastline, France Spain Morocco and Senegal labelled. Long silky multicolour semitransparent milky heat fields along Europe-to-west-Africa corridor, visible underlying terrain, broad diffuse outer mist and luminous core, fine microscopic strand contours from reference. The right panel heading "A journey, collected." and a spectacular full-size, near-front-facing postage CARD at centre, about 290x420px: WHITE STORK illustrated with elegant engraved feather detail on deep blue paper, cream perforated border, embossed pale gold typography and subtle angular polychrome laminate. Full card legible, thickness slight, not floating toy. Below card a segmented finish picker "Original" "Foil" "Holo" "Polychrome" with Polychrome selected and a compact action "Save to collection". Two small species stamp thumbnails below labelled "Latham’s snipe" and "Red-necked stint". On map bottom a functional time scrubber with months and September selected. Map legend and note visible. A thin vertical divider, sophisticated layout, gallery-quality material, foil material clearly visible but bird illustration dominates. Strong map AND card detail coexist, calm type, no extra boxes.
